 Delhi thrash Punjab by 109 runs; Saurashtra crush Haryana by 6 wickets in Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy
 PTI

 Indore, Nov 16 (PTI) Yash Dhull’s unbeaten 40-ball 78 and Mayank Yadav’s four-wicket burst powered Delhi to a 109-run over Punjab in a Elite Group B match of the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy at Holkar stadium here on Monday.
 Sent in to bat, Dhull hammered seven fours and five sixes, while captain Priyansh Arya laid the foundation with a 32-ball 55, studded with four fours and three sixes as Delhi posted a mammoth 240 for five.
 Nitish Rana (35 off 20), Sarthak Ranjan (25 off 14), and Tejasvi Dahiya (20 off 10) also chipped in, before Himmat Singh blasted two sixes in his four-ball 13.
 Show Full Article
 For Punjab, Sukhdeep Bajwa (2/43) and Sahil Bhaskar (2/46) took two wickets as their attack also leaked 13 wides.
 Chasing a daunting 241, Punjab were bowled out for 131 in 17.5 overs.
 Vihaan Malhotra (23 off 10) and Anmolpreet Singh (27) gave them a brisk start, but Mayank derailed the chase.
 The pacer dismissed Malhotra, Uday Saharan, and Arjun Rajput, the last two for ducks, and returned later to remove Bajwa, finishing with 4/12 in three overs which included a maiden.
 Captain Ramandeep Singh (30) and Harpreet Brar (33) offered some resistance, but spinner Digvesh Singh Rathi (3/21) wrapped up the innings.
 J&K beat TN by six runs
 ==================
 In another match, opener Qamran Iqbal smashed a 37-ball 70 as Jammu and Kashmir held their nerve to beat Tamil Nadu by six runs.
 After opting to bat, J&K posted 201 for seven, built on Iqbal’s blistering knock that included 10 fours and three sixes.
 Skipper Shubham Khajuria added a 34-ball 53 with four sixes, while Abdul Samad provided the late flourish with a 14-ball 29.
 For Tamil Nadu, V Athisayaraj Davidson (2/49) and captain R Sai Kishore (2/36) took two wickets each.
 In reply, Tamil Nadu lost Tushar Raheja for a duck, but Amit Sathvik kept them in the hunt with a fiery 67 off 31 balls, studded with nine fours and three sixes.
 Narayan Jagadeesan (35 off 20) and Balasubramaniam Sachin (29) chipped in, and R Rajkumar’s 10-ball 24 kept the contest alive in the closing overs.
 However, Tamil Nadu kept losing wickets at regular intervals and finished on 195 for nine.
 Saurashtra crush Haryana by six wickets 
 ==============================
 At the Daly College Ground, Vishvaraj Jadeja’s 23-ball 46 helped Saurashtra crush Haryana by six wickets in another Group B match.
 Chasing a modest 119, Saurashtra raced to the target in 13.5 overs, after Jadeja and Harvik Desai (24 off 19) put on 60 for the opening wicket inside six overs.
 Jadeja struck three fours and four sixes during his blistering knock.
 Leg-spinner Yuzvendra Chahal (3/27) gave Haryana brief hope, removing Desai and Harvansh Pangalia off successive deliveries in the sixth over and later bowling Sammar Gajjar for a duck. Saurashtra slipped from 60 without loss to 85 for four.
 However, Prerak Mankad (28 not out) and Ruchit Ahir (21 not out) shared an unbroken 34-run stand to see their side home without further fuss.
 Earlier, Haryana were restricted to 118 for nine after they opted to bat. Wicketkeeper-batter Yashvardhan Dalal kept the innings together with an unbeaten 65 off 54 balls, hitting seven fours and a six.
 Rahul Tewatia (14) was the other batter to reach double digits as the Saurashtra bowling unit, led by skipper Jaydev Unadkat (2/19), produced a disciplined effort.
 Parth Bhut was the most economical with 2/13 in four overs, and Chetan Sakariya also took two wickets.
 Bihar beat Railways by four wickets
 ==========================
 At the same venue, Bihar registered a four-wicket win over Railways in another match, riding on opener Ayush Loharuka’s 29-ball 58 and three wickets apiece for Prashant Singh (3/28) and Suraj Kashyap (3/29).
 Asked to take first strike, Railways could manage just 137 for nine with opener Jayant Lakhan (47), Ravi Singh (21) and Zubair Ali Khan (26) doing bulk of the scoring.
 But Prashant polished the three top-order batters and then Kashyap rocked the middle order with another three wickets. Mohammed Izhar (2/18) also snapped two late order batters to rob Railways of any momentum.
 In reply, Loharuka smashed five sixes and as many fours to give Bihar a rollicking start. By the time he was dismissed hit-wicket, Bihar were 78 for 2 in 8.2 overs.
 Contributions from Tarun Kumar (20), Altamish Ashraf (15), Raghuvendra Pratap Singh (18) and Kashyap (13) helped them to complete the chase, scoring 141/6 in 18.2 overs.
 Brief scores:
 Delhi: 240/5 in 20 overs (Yash Dhull 78 not out, Priyansh Arya 55; Sukhdeep Bajwa 2/43, Sahil Bhaskar 2/46) beat Punjab: 131 all out in 17.5 overs (Harpreet Brar 33, Ramandeep Singh 30; Mayank Yadav 4/12, Digvesh Singh Rathi 3/21) by 109 runs.
 Jammu and Kashmir: 201/7 in 20 overs (Qamran Iqbal 70, Shubham Khajuria 53; R Sai Kishore 2/36, V Athisayaraj Davidson 2/49) beat Tamil Nadu: 195/9 in 20 overs (Amit Sathvik 67, Narayan Jagadeesan 35; Lone Nasir Muzaffar 3/42, Brijesh Sharma 2/31, Sunil Kumar 2/32) by 6 runs.
 Haryana: 118/9 in 20 overs (Yashvardhan Dalal 65 not out; Parth Bhut 2/13, Jaydev Unadkat 2/19, Chetan Sakariya 2/39) lost to Saurashtra: 119/4 in 13.5 overs (Vishvaraj Jadeja 46, Prerak Mankad 28 not out; Yuzvendra Chahal 3/27) by 6 wickets.
 Railways: 137/9 in 20 overs (Jayant Lakhan 47; Prashant Singh 3/28, Suraj Kashyap 3/29, Mohammed Izhar 2/18) lost to Bihar: 141/6 in 18.2 overs (Ayush Loharuka 58, Tarun Kumar 20, Raghuvendra Pratap Singh 18; Mohammad Saif 2/17) by 4 wickets PTI ATK DDV
